node.title: L1 partial-pullback Johnson router
node.statement: For one monic degree-s map, let B be its b complete domain-fiber labels, let k_j=ceil((k-j)/s), and let kappa=sum_j max(0,k_j-b). For a listed codeword, let z count agreement points not contained in a fully agreed complete fiber. Then |Agr|=s|E|+z exactly. Under z<=Z, the quotient tuple agrees on at least h_Z=ceil((k+ell-1-Z)/s) labels. If h_Z^2>b(ceil(k/s)-1), a direct interleaved Johnson count bounds the class by q^kappa b^2 per map. Under a tame whole-petal anchor, fixed kappa<=K, and q<=n^gamma, all map classes cost at most n^(3+gamma K). This theorem leaves the nonpositive gate, kernel, wild maps, and missing anchors; the later coverage/kernel tradeoff proves kappa<=max(0,z-ell+1), absorbing the kernel into growing partial loss. The exact F_17^* affine-quadratic witness has z=5, kappa=0, and lies on the nonpositive side.
